policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'a great voice out of the throne', so θρόνου and not οὐρανοῦ is the text it rendered.
ASV's plural 'they shall be his peoples' reflects λαοί rather than the singular λαός.

ASV reads 'God himself shall be with them, and be their God' and footnotes 'Some ancient authorities omit, and be their God', an explicit mapped note keeping αὐτῶν θεός in the text; the order also matches μετ᾽ αὐτῶν ἔσται.
ἐκ and ἀπό are both 'from' before τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν, and ASV 'from their eyes' is identical under either.

ASV joins with a colon and no conjunction — 'nor pain, any more: the first things are passed away' — while rendering ὅτι as 'for' in the next verse, which excludes r02's ὅτι; the base and r01 differ only in punctuation, so the base fallback is retained.
καινὰ ποιῶ πάντα and πάντα καινὰ ποιῶ differ only in order, and ASV 'I make all things new' fixes that order by its own syntax.
ASV reads 'And he saith, Write' with no indirect object, while rendering the μοι of the next verse as 'And he said unto me', so its text lacked the added μοι.
ASV 'these words are faithful and true' follows πιστοὶ καὶ ἀληθινοί rather than RP's reversed pair.

ASV's plural 'They are come to pass' reflects γέγοναν and excludes RP's singular γέγονα, but English requires a copula in 'I am the Alpha' whether or not εἰμι stands, and the base and r01 differ only in punctuation, so the base fallback is retained.
ASV lists 'the fearful, and unbelieving, and abominable' with nothing answering RP's added καὶ ἁμαρτωλοῖς.

ASV's personal relative 'seven angels who had the seven bowls, who were laden with the seven last plagues' refers the second clause to the angels, matching masculine genitive τῶν γεμόντων rather than γεμούσας agreeing with the bowls.
ASV 'the bride, the wife of the Lamb' follows νύμφην τὴν γυναῖκα rather than RP's reversed nouns.
ASV reads 'the holy city Jerusalem' with nothing answering RP's added τὴν μεγάλην, though it renders that phrase as 'the great city' elsewhere in Revelation.
ἐπὶ τοῖς πυλῶσιν and ἐπὶ τοὺς πυλῶνας are both 'at the gates', and ASV does not report the case.
ASV italicizes 'the names' in 'which are the names of the twelve tribes' as a supply, so its text read the bare ἅ ἐστιν without ὀνόματα.
The variant is only an additional article before φυλῶν, and ASV 'of the twelve tribes' is identical under either.
ἀνατολῆς and ἀνατολῶν are singular and plural of the same noun, both rendered 'on the east'.
ἔχων and ἔχον differ only in the gender of the participle, and ASV 'had twelve foundations' shows no agreement.
The added καί after ὅσον is adverbial, which ASV's 'as great as the breadth' would leave unrendered in either case.
σταδίους and σταδίων differ only in case after ἐπί, and ASV 'twelve thousand furlongs' does not report it.
ASV reads 'twelve thousand furlongs' with a single twelve, so its text had δώδεκα χιλιάδων without RP's second δώδεκα.
English requires a copula in 'the city was pure gold' whether or not ἦν stands in the Greek.
ASV begins verse 19 'The foundations of the wall of the city were adorned' with no conjunction, while opening most verses of this chapter with 'And' for καί, so its text lacked Treg's καί.

ASV 'the kings of the earth bring their glory into it' answers τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν and has nothing for RP's καὶ τιμὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν, which it does render as 'the glory and the honor of the nations' where the Greek has it in verse 26.
ASV's personal 'he that maketh an abomination' excludes the neuter ποιοῦν agreeing with πᾶν κοινόν, but a bare participle and an articular ὁ ποιῶν are both rendered by that relative clause.
